source.title: Perturbed Gradients Updating within Unit Space for Deep Learning
source.authors: Ching-Hsun Tseng; Hsueh-Cheng Liu; Shin-Jye Lee; Xiaojun Zeng

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present, though some equations and table entries are garbled in the supplied extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers and reports held-out image-classification accuracy and train/test loss gaps, using a different optimizer intervention from the versions' cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons and train/test loss histories that bear on V4 and V7. It does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, architecture comparisons of convolutional versus fully connected networks, batch size, dropout, or removal of memorized examples. The loss-gap plots are figure-only; the text describes their qualitative trends.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adagrad with SGD on held-out CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 accuracy, bearing on V4 under a fixed, minimally tuned recipe. PUGD performance and qualitative landscape visualizations do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness ranking.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors argue that PUGD provides locally bounded updates and sharpness awareness, reaches flat minima in their visualizations, and outperforms their optimizer comparators. They describe competitive CIFAR results and claim state-of-the-art Tiny ImageNet finetuning performance as of June 29, 2021.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces PUGD, a unit-gradient optimizer with perturbation, and compares it against SGD, adaptive methods, NGD variants, SAM, ASAM, and AMP; this is not the original intervention for the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, optimizer, model architecture, and epoch count vary across results. The CIFAR-10 history comparison uses batch size 100 and different epoch counts for perturbated and non-perturbated optimizers.

fits_no_version.finding: PUGD improves held-out accuracy over SGD across the reported architectures and datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under this study's fixed recipe, PUGD outperforms SGD on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors describe PUGD as producing smoother landscapes and more stable late training than several competitors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Qualitative landscape and optimization-history comparisons favor PUGD in these experiments.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
record.problems: Loss histories and landscapes are presented as figures without extractable numeric values. End-to-end tables report test accuracy but not training accuracy or train/test gaps. The CIFAR-100 AMP table entry is garbled, and the text notes different epoch counts for perturbated and non-perturbated optimizers.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of learned local connectivity.
Adam and other adaptive methods beyond Adagrad; language benchmarks; equal or better training performance; learning-rate tuning, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching to SGD.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout interventions and interactions with data size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of highly memorized training examples versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The decisive V4 evidence is the omitted Adagrad-versus-SGD accuracy comparison, not PUGD's advantage. All optimizers receive a common learning rate rather than individually tuned learning rates, limiting the conclusion to that recipe. Missing V7 measurements warrant an untested entry, not a limits_scope verdict. Optimizer names throughout the record should not be typed as models; the architectures identify the trained models.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their test-error effects.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive methods' breadth across image and language benchmarks; broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers; word-level language models.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interaction with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurement and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures; study uses qualitative loss landscapes and training histories instead.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 and compared through training and test loss histories over 200 epochs.
rows.measure: Training and test loss histories; qualitative train/test gap and test loss

rows.note: Qualitative description in text; no numerical loss values supplied.
rows.check: High loss alone does not establish worse held-out performance than SGD; the relevant numerical comparisons are omitted from Tables IV–V. Adagrad is an optimizer, not a model.

relationships.condition: Adagrad versus momentum SGD on four architectures, CIFAR-10; learning rate 0.1, cosine schedule, weight decay 0.0005, 200 epochs.
relationships.reason: Based on Table IV's omitted Adagrad results, accuracy is lower for every architecture: 91.11/90.49/89.03/91.57% versus SGD's 93.99/95.60/94.81/95.03% in R9, R11, R13, R15.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower Adagrad accuracy than momentum SGD across the four CIFAR-10 architectures remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Adagrad versus momentum SGD on four architectures, CIFAR-100; the same fixed recipe and 200 epochs.
relationships.reason: Based on Table V's omitted Adagrad results, accuracy is lower for every architecture: 60.68/64.85/61.21/68.22% versus SGD's 74.18/78.42/76.08/76.07% in R18, R20, R22, R24.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower Adagrad accuracy than momentum SGD across the four CIFAR-100 architectures remains unverified.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: UPANet16 on CIFAR-10; VGG-16, ResNet-18, DenseNet121*, and UPANet-16 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports optimizer-dependent test performance, with PUGD outperforming the listed competitors in its tables and a smaller qualitative loss gap late in training (R1–R25). It does not establish the adaptive-optimizer claim across the benchmarks or tuning regimes named in V4.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The qualitative loss-gap comparison favors PUGD late in training, but the paper does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or rank it against norm- and margin-based measures (R26–R29).
